input.symptom_description: compressor current spike then drops to zero, compressor state fault, cabin temperature rising above setpoint

input.description: Telemetry shows stable operation (~11-12A) until 20:10, when compressor_current_a spiked to 24A, then collapsed to 0A with compressor_state flipping to "fault" at 20:20 and remaining there through the end of the window. Cabin temp has since risen steadily from 2.0°C to 4.8°C, above the 2°C setpoint, with controller_reading_c tracking cabin_temp_c exactly at every sample (no divergence). KB-003 (temperature drift) explicitly states that a diagnostic reset only applies when the controller reading diverges from the cabin probe (sensor calibration drift); when the controller tracks the cabin probe as it does here, the refrigeration circuit itself is at fault and requires a technician. Combined with the overcurrent spike and sustained fault state (consistent with a compressor trip, not a sensor issue), this points to a real mechanical/electrical compressor fault rather than a software/calibration issue. No other KB entries or service history exist to contradict this, so recommending a service visit as the cautious option rather than a remote reset.
